content:
Yesterday we studied the beginning of the manna; how Yahweh rained bread from heaven, what it looked like, what it tasted like, and how it came down with the dew each night. We ended with a puzzle. On ordinary days, no one was allowed to keep any manna until the morning. Yet on one day of the week, that very rule was reversed. Today we find the answer, and we continue the wonderful history of this bread from heaven.

First we must see what happened when the people disobeyed the daily rule. Yahweh instructed them not to keep any ordinary manna until the next day. Exodus 16:19 says that no one should keep any of it until morning. But some of the people did not obey. They saved some of it overnight, perhaps out of fear about the next day. And Exodus 16:20 says, "By then it was full of maggots and had a terrible smell". The manna spoiled because they had disobeyed Yahweh's command. This showed the people that they had to depend upon Yahweh every single day. They were not permitted to gather a large amount and store it up because they were afraid about the future. Each day Yahweh gave them exactly what they needed for that day, and each day they had to trust Him again for the next.

Then comes the answer to yesterday's puzzle, and it is beautiful. Manna came on six days of the week, but on the sixth day Yahweh told the people to gather twice as much as usual. Exodus 16:22 says, "On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much as usual". Instead of one omer for each person, they gathered two. Moses explained that the seventh day would be the Sabbath, a holy day of rest, and that no manna would come on that day. So the people were to prepare the food on the sixth day and keep enough for the Sabbath. Now normally, manna spoiled when it was kept overnight. But the manna kept from the sixth day did not spoil at all. Exodus 16:24 says, "In the morning the leftover food was wholesome and good, without maggots or odor". This was another miracle. The very same food that rotted on ordinary days remained fresh and good when it was kept according to Yahweh's command. The difference was never in the manna itself. The difference was obedience to the word of God.

On the seventh day, some of the people still went out to look for manna, but they found none. Exodus 16:25 says, "There will be no food on the ground today". So the manna came from the first day through the sixth day, but it did not come on the seventh. The people had to trust Yahweh's instruction and gather the double portion on the sixth day, or they would go hungry on the Sabbath. In this simple pattern of bread, God was teaching His people to honour the day of rest He had set apart, and to trust that His provision on the sixth day would be enough to carry them through the seventh.

God also commanded Moses to preserve a portion of the manna as a lasting memorial. Exodus 16:32 says, "Fill a two-quart container with manna to preserve it for your descendants". Aaron was told to place the jar before Yahweh, so that future generations could see the very food God had used to feed Israel in the wilderness. Later this jar of manna was connected with the Ark of the Covenant, for Hebrews 9:4 speaks of "a gold jar containing manna". This preserved manna did not spoil like ordinary manna. Ordinary manna rotted overnight when people kept it against God’s command, but the manna placed before God remained preserved, because God commanded it to be kept as a testimony. The power was never in the jar itself. The preservation was by the will of God. And so this jar became a witness to all the later generations that God had faithfully fed His people during their journey through the wilderness.

Israel ate manna throughout the whole wilderness journey. Exodus 16:35 says, "The people of Israel ate manna for forty years". For forty years, Yahweh provided food for the entire nation. Every day, except the Sabbath, manna appeared upon the ground. On the sixth day, a double amount came. On the seventh day, none came at all. And this continued year after year after year. Children were born in the wilderness and grew up eating manna. Families travelled from place to place and were sustained by the same heavenly provision. Yahweh did not give manna for only a few days or a few weeks.

He continued feeding them faithfully for the entire journey, never once forgetting them, never once failing to provide.

The manna continued until Israel entered the land of Canaan. When they crossed the Jordan and came into the Promised Land, they began to eat the food produced in that land. Joshua 5:11-12 says, "No manna appeared on the day they first ate from the crops of the land, and it was never seen again". The manna stopped because its purpose had been completed. While Israel was in the wilderness, they had no fields of their own and no regular harvest,

so Yahweh fed them with manna. But once they entered Canaan and ate the produce of the land, the manna was no longer needed. The day before, manna had been their food. The next day, it stopped forever. For forty years Yahweh had sustained them, and when they reached the Promised Land, He simply provided for them in a new way. His care did not end; it only changed its form.

For forty years, the manna stood as a daily witness that Yahweh had not forgotten His people. In a dry land where food could not naturally be found for so great a multitude, Yahweh provided enough for every family, every person, and every day of the journey. The rich lessons of the manna for the New Creation, God willing, we will study in tomorrow's Morning Light.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God,

We stand amazed at Your faithfulness; forty years without one missing morning.

You fed a whole nation in a barren land and provided enough for every household.

Teach us to honour the rest You have set apart, and to trust Your provision for it.

Help us to obey Your word, for it is obedience, not our own effort, that keeps our portion fresh.

And when the manna of one season ends, help us to trust that You will provide in a new way.

"Great is his faithfulness; his mercies begin afresh each morning." Lamentations 3:23

In the name of Christ, the true bread from heaven, we pray. Amen.
